input: s is a string consisting only of ASCII digits 0 through 9, with length in [0, 4294967295]. Lengths outside [4, 12] return an empty result immediately. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh list of every valid dotted-decimal IPv4 address obtained by inserting exactly three dots into s without removing, changing or reordering digits. Each of four components is in [0, 255], and leading zeroes are forbidden except for the component "0". Results follow depth-first increasing component-length order and contain no duplicates. Impossible or out-of-range lengths return a fresh empty sequence.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. The temporary parts sequence is private. Returned strings are immutable and freshly assembled in a fresh outer container; no mutable alias to parts escapes. String-identity freshness is not promised.
numeric: At most three digits are parsed for a component. The expression value*10 + characterCode - 48 has intermediate value at most 1047 and final value at most 999 before the >255 check. The four-component depth is at most five live calls, and all indices used after the initial length check are at most 15. No whole-input integer parsing or numeric overflow occurs.
complexity: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space under the fixed four-component IPv4 grammar, including the immediate length rejection. There are at most 3^4 = 81 candidate leaf length assignments, helper depth at most five, and component copies of at most three characters. Retained output is O(R) strings/slots, R <= 81, each string at most 15 characters; these copies and joins are explicitly charged. Input-string length retrieval is constant-time for the declared ordinary string runtimes.

helpers.name: collect
helpers.contract: A bounded choose/recurse/undo closure. First prune when remaining digits cannot fit remaining slots; at zero slots, join parts. Otherwise try component lengths one through three, reject a leading zero continuation or value above 255, copy the component slice, recurse and undo.
helpers.cost: The full helper definition is 679 UTF-8 bytes including indentation and terminal newline, already included in source bytes. At most five live calls. Every digit read, copied component, join and result string is included in the bounded costs.
